A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides; no paired leaves or whorls observed)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (multiple leaves appear grouped at the distal end of the stem, forming a terminal cluster)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf has a single blade attached to the petiole; no leaflets present)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no teeth or serrations visible)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest near the middle, tapering to both ends, with a generally oval form)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (tapering to a narrow base, wedge-shaped)

    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is relatively short, not exceeding the leaf blade length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (round in cross-section, not flattened or winged)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears soft and green, not woody)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)

    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no ridges or lenticels visible; surface appears smooth)
